slides.headline: EVERY AI TOOL YOU USE HAS 5 DEFAULT SETTINGS QUIETLY SENDING YOUR WORK TO THEIR SERVERS
slides.kicker: Two lawsuits this week prove it

slides.headline: 1) TURN OFF THE SETTING THAT TRAINS AI ON YOUR WORK
slides.body:
Samsung engineers leaked confidential chip code through ChatGPT in 2023.

Samsung banned employee AI use company-wide after the story broke.

Your business is probably doing what Samsung's team did the day before.

slides.headline: 2) CHECK WHAT THE DEFAULT TERMS SAY ABOUT YOUR CONTENT
slides.body:
ChatGPT's default terms give OpenAI a license to use your outputs to improve its models.

The next product launch you draft in AI might be training the model your competitor uses tomorrow.

slides.headline: 3) LIMIT WHAT YOUR EMAIL AI CAN READ AND KEEP
slides.body:
Copilot for Outlook and Gmail AI both request read access to your full inbox history by default.

Every email, including confidential negotiations, becomes accessible to the AI and its parent company.
Per song. That is what Sony is seeking from Anthropic for training on content without permission. Every AI tool that collects your business data by default is making the same trade with your work

slides.headline: 4) ADD A FACT-CHECK LAYER BEFORE AI ANSWERS YOUR CUSTOMERS
slides.body:
Air Canada's AI chatbot gave a passenger the wrong refund policy.

A court held Air Canada legally responsible for what the bot said.

If your AI answers customers, you own every mistake it makes.

slides.headline: 5) FIND OUT HOW LONG YOUR AI TOOL KEEPS EVERYTHING YOU TYPE
slides.body:
The Apple case this week showed messages sent months ago can be retrieved and used in court.

Everything you type into an AI tool sits on a server somewhere, often for months or years.

slides.headline: SAVE THIS: 5 AI SETTINGS TO CHECK TONIGHT
slides.body:
1. Turn off training data collection
2. Know who owns your AI content
3. Limit email AI inbox access
4. Add a fact-check to customer AI
5. Find data retention policy

Daily AI news

caption:
Swipe before your next AI session. 5 default settings quietly working against your business right now, with prompts to fix each one tonight. 🔒

Training data opt-out, the setting most business owners never touch. Default terms that may license your content back to the AI company. Email AI access scope, what it reads beyond your inbox. A fact-check layer for customer-facing AI, how to add it tonight. Data retention, how long your conversations stay on their servers and what to do about it

Two AI lawsuits landed this week and a Berlin artist proved that AI cameras have blind spots a single shirt can exploit. The same gaps exist in every tool your business trusts with data right now. These prompts take under ten minutes each and can all be run tonight.

Running a business? DM us "AI" and we'll show you what this could do for yours.

Sources: Sony Music filing Sep 2026, Apple court filing Sep 2026, US Copyright Office, Air Canada v. Moffatt 2024, Simon Weckert research
